short: The lead ship of the Soviet Typhoon class, the largest submarines ever built.
full:
Commissioned on 29 December 1981, TK-208 Dmitriy Donskoy was the lead ship of the Project 941 Akula (Typhoon) class, the largest submarines ever constructed. Designed to operate under the Arctic ice cap, the colossal vessel displaced nearly 48,000 tonnes submerged and carried twenty massive R-39 solid-fuel ballistic missiles. Its unique multi-hulled design provided exceptional survivability and buoyancy, allowing it to easily break through thick pack ice to launch its payload.

The Typhoon class represented the zenith of Soviet strategic naval power during the Cold War, serving as a highly visible and heavily armed maritime deterrent. Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, most of the class was retired due to enormous operating costs. Dmitriy Donskoy, however, was extensively modernised and served as a testbed for the new Bulava missile system, remaining in the Russian Navy until its official decommissioning on 6 February 2023.
